authorityBoundary: Every profile is Target — planned, not executable. It defines intended decision structure but creates no command, implementation, approval, release, operational, security, privacy, compliance, audit, or certification authority.

plannedSubsteps: Inspect bounded user, business, domain, and Source evidence; keep unsupported assumptions Unknown.
Facilitate challenge and prepare a traceable candidate model or decision.
Have the accountable business role review exact evidence, limitations, and exit criteria before a future governed commit.
Assess classification, applicability, policy, jurisdiction, and risk evidence.
Prepare explicit decisions, exclusions, open questions, assurance triggers, and escalation owners.
Block the governed decision until one accountable role and required independent assurance review the exact scope.
Inspect domain, architecture, quality, risk, deployment, and evidence constraints for the affected slice.
Compare alternatives and prepare traceable models, decisions, quality scenarios, and assurance requirements.
Obtain accountable architecture decision and required independent challenge; preserve rejected alternatives and residual risks.
Inspect current architecture, Product evidence, constraints, dependencies, and readiness criteria.
Prepare tool-neutral Product Design, vertical-slice, backlog, acceptance, dependency, and test candidates with traceability.
Reconcile challenge evidence and obtain the bounded accountable product/engineering decision without granting implementation authority.
Resolve repository topology, implementation targets, dependencies, authority, and protected evidence boundaries.
Execute only authorized bounded changes and collect code, scan, test, traceability, and drift evidence.
Separate product acceptance, implementation/repository authority, release/change authorization, and deployment evidence.
Observe service, environment, user, incident, recovery, risk, and outcome evidence with exact scope and freshness.
Respond and recover under operational authority while preserving material decisions and evidence.
Feed validated observations into a newly bounded Product/Initiative change; never rewrite prior governed intent silently.

questions: What problem and outcome are evidenced?
What remains assumption?
exitCriteria: Intent, outcomes, exclusions, assumptions, and evidence are reviewable

questions: What exact content and revision was reviewed?
What Baseline/Provenance/revalidation changes are required?
exitCriteria: Source, Baseline, Provenance, and change effects remain distinct and explicit

questions: What durable Product and bounded change are in scope?
exitCriteria: Stable identities, scope, outcomes, constraints, and exclusions are reviewable

questions: Which classifications and controls apply?
Who can decide exclusions and accept risk?
exitCriteria: Applicability, exceptions, assurance triggers, and open questions have accountable dispositions

questions: What user/business outcomes and assumptions require discovery?
exitCriteria: Discovery claims trace to evidence and unresolved assumptions remain visible

questions: Which capabilities/value streams/rules change?
exitCriteria: Business model and decisions support domain/solution work

questions: Which domain events, commands, policies, actors, and hotspots matter?
exitCriteria: Events/hotspots are traceable and contested interpretations explicit

questions: Which bounded contexts, ownership, and relationships fit the evidence?
blockers: DDD treated as automatic microservices prescription
exitCriteria: Boundaries and alternatives are explicit without deployment-style inflation

questions: Which architecture style and deployment model fit?
exitCriteria: Affected-slice architecture is sufficient before backlog finalization

questions: What decision, alternative, tradeoff, assurance, and review trigger are required?
exitCriteria: Decision rationale, alternatives, residual risks, and verification criteria are governed

questions: Which phases, waves, Products, and vertical slices deliver evidence safely?
exitCriteria: Sequence and dependencies are traceable to outcomes and architecture

questions: What Product Design evidence is needed and how will adapters reconcile?
outputs: Tool-neutral Product Design candidate and reconciliation evidence
blockers: Figma treated as lifecycle stage or authority
exitCriteria: Design evidence is tool-neutral, reviewed, traceable, and iterative

questions: Which Epics/Features/Stories/tests/dependencies/DoR/DoD form an architecture-bound slice?
exitCriteria: Backlog, tests, traceability, repository target, and readiness criteria align

questions: Which mono/polyrepo and implementation targets own each change?
blockers: GAEP-P03-GAP-001 unresolved for required target type
exitCriteria: Each slice maps to explicit projects/repositories/owners without granting mutation authority

questions: How will cross-repository distribution, synchronization, traceability, and drift work?
Which agents may change what, under whose repository authority, with which evidence?
exitCriteria: Authorized changes and evidence are traceable; no agent self-approves

questions: Does the stated Product slice meet bounded acceptance criteria and who can accept it?
outputs: QA findings and product acceptance decision
exitCriteria: QA and acceptance are explicit and separate from release authority

questions: Who authorizes release/deployment and what rollback/evidence is required?
exitCriteria: Release and deployment decisions are scoped, auditable, and reversible

questions: What happened, what authority governs response, and what Product change is now justified?
outputs: Operational evidence and bounded feedback Initiative
blockers: Missing operational authority or evidence retention
exitCriteria: Response/recovery is documented and learning re-enters Product governance explicitly
